source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Verify can install OS with TPM  device enable.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria: Verify can install OS with TPM  device enable.

deepseek_columns.ai_packages_needed: OS installer media (user provides) + tpm2-tools (post-OS check)
deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- TPM linux command (OS install with TPM enabled): verifying a clean OS install with TPM on is a long OS-install task the agent can stage (boot to installer) but needs the installer media + interaction; agent can verify the installed OS sees the TPM via sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "ls /dev/tpm0 2>&1; dmesg 2>&1 | grep -i tpm; systemd-cryptenroll --tpm2-device list 2>&1" afterwards.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return the post-install OS TPM detection (tpm0, dmesg, cryptenroll device list) so the user confirms TPM works with the installed OS.
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: OS install repartitions the disk; run only on a dedicated SUT/drive the user designates.

original_test_intent: Install the approved OS while TPM is enabled and prove successful installation, boot and the project-defined TPM functionality in the installed OS.
original_method: After an owner verifies a dedicated disposable disk by stable identity, signed OS image and TPM/UEFI policy, an unattended controller installs only that target, captures installer/partition/boot evidence, boots the new OS and collects platform-tolerant TPM/security validation before approved cleanup or retention.
manual_activity: A user must designate the image and exact disposable disk and approve the unchanged destructive plan. With supported virtual media/PXE/unattended installation, the normal core does not require physical or visual human operation.
required_inputs: Signed OS image/version/hash, installer mode and license
Dedicated disposable disk stable serial/WWN and full storage exclusion inventory
TPM enabled state, UEFI/Secure Boot/measured-boot policy
Unattended partition/install profile and post-install TPM acceptance
OOB/virtual-media recovery, backup/reimage/final-state plan and one-user approval
safety_requirements: Never infer `/dev/sda`, NVMe index or any target; match the approved stable identity at execution time.
Do not clear/re-own TPM or alter keys unless separately authorized.
Stop before writes on any identity mismatch and stop on first install/boot/security anomaly; no automatic retry.
agent_execution_scope: Perform pre-write storage identity and exclusion checks, then run only the approved unattended install against the designated target.
Capture installer, partition, boot and post-install TPM/device/properties/security evidence.
Verify non-target storage unchanged and report tool results without engineer verdict.
engineer_actions: Designate and approve the exact disposable target, image and TPM acceptance.
Approve recovery/final state and any exceptional intervention.
Review evidence and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Post-install checks are supporting evidence but fixed `/dev/tpm0` is not portable and the proposal does not implement target-safe installation.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the project's validated unattended installer/PXE/virtual-media workflow and platform-tolerant TPM checks only after stable target verification.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: OS installation with TPM enabled and the 5/20-minute source fields are preserved; actual project duration may be overridden and reported.

modernized_recommendation.status: USE TARGET-LOCKED UNATTENDED INSTALL AFTER OWNER INPUTS
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Bind an immutable install manifest to image hash and disk serial/WWN, enforce protected-device exclusions, capture installer logs and validate TPM identity/properties and boot policy in the installed OS.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Approved SUT, firmware, installer and disposable storage target.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BIOS/TPM firmware, installer/image, provisioning system, OS/kernel and tpm2-tools versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Owner OS provisioning, storage safety and TPM/boot acceptance specifications.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds deterministic target/image identity and automated end-to-end evidence.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No loss; installation and TPM-enabled boot remain required.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Image, stable target, policy, unattended profile and recovery.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Execution readiness remains NOT READY until the destructive target is positively identified; that is not permanent BLOCKED.

project_override_considerations: The project selects image, disposable target, TPM acceptance and cleanup. Completion applies only to that approved plan; no original or alternate disk coverage may be claimed.
expected_evidence: Image hash, target serial/WWN, storage inventory/exclusions, TPM/UEFI policy and authorization
Installer/partition/boot logs proving writes stayed on the target
Post-install TPM device/properties, driver and project-defined security/boot checks
Non-target integrity, host/BMC health, cleanup/final state and separate engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Title is imprecise but the procedure and criterion consistently require installing an OS with TPM enabled.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Missing image, target and TPM criteria make execution not ready but are explicitly project-supplied inputs under V3.1, not permanent BLOCKED.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Reclassify from PARTIAL because media/target confirmation does not make an unattended core manual.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Reject permanent BLOCKED caused by missing project inputs while retaining all storage safety gates.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Separates destructive readiness, automated execution status and engineer verdict.

review_improvement: Defines target-locked end-to-end installation and TPM evidence without guessing a disk or weakening the no-write safety invariant.
independent_technical_reasoning: Provisioning systems can automate boot media, partitioning, OS installation, reboot and validation. The exact image and disposable target must be confirmed, but those inputs affect readiness rather than automation capability.
